# Twilio Studio TypeScript SDK (unofficial)

Unofficial TypeScript SDK for the Twilio Studio API, version 2.

The `TwilioStudio` client is generated by flowapi from the API's description: 19 methods in 5 resources, each listed in [api.md](api.md) with its parameters and what it returns.

## Install

```sh
npm install twilio-studio-sdk
```

## Usage

```ts
import { TwilioStudio } from 'twilio-studio-sdk'

const client = new TwilioStudio()

const result = await client.flows.list()
console.log(result)
```

A method takes its operation's parameters in one object, grouped by where each goes (`path`, `query`, `header`, `cookie`), with a body as `body: { contentType, value }`; it gives the response's body, read as the description says. A second argument changes one call (`headers`, `query`, `timeout`, `maxRetries`, `signal`). `withResponse()` gives the body with the raw response and the server's request id, `asResponse()` the raw response alone.

```ts
const { data, response, requestId } = await client.flows.list().withResponse()
console.log(response.status, requestId, data)
```

The package is built twice, as ES modules and as CommonJS, each with its types, and depends on nothing: it calls the platform's `fetch`. From CommonJS the client is taken by its name, `const { TwilioStudio } = require('twilio-studio-sdk')`; `import TwilioStudio from 'twilio-studio-sdk'` gives it too.

## Authentication

| Scheme | Kind | Sent as | Option | Environment variables |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accountSid_authToken` | HTTP basic | `Authorization: Basic <base64 of user-id:password, UTF-8>` | `accountSidAuthToken`: `{ username, password }` (a user-id without `:`) | `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`: the user-id; `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`: the password |

An operation's security is a list of alternatives: the client sends the first one it holds every credential of, and an operation that needs none sends none. Each credential is an option of the client, else read from its environment variables when a call needs it; a call none of whose alternatives can be met throws `CredentialError`, naming the options and variables, before anything is sent. Credentials go only over `https:`, or to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`: elsewhere a call over plain `http:` throws `InsecureCredentialError`, unless the client is given `allowInsecureCredentials: true`. The log writes each as `***`, and a redirect to another origin is not followed unless `allowCrossOriginRedirects` is set, and then without them.

```ts
const client = new TwilioStudio({ accountSidAuthToken: { username: '…', password: '…' } })
```

## Environments

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| `production` | https://studio.twilio.com |

The client calls `production` unless it is given `environment` or `baseURL`, or `TWILIO_STUDIO_BASE_URL` is set.

## Errors

A response whose status is not a success throws an `APIError` with its `status`, `headers`, `body` and `requestId`, of the class for its status (any other status is an `APIError` itself):

| Status | Class |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `BadRequestError` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationError` |
| 403 | `PermissionDeniedError` |
| 404 | `NotFoundError` |
| 408 | `RequestTimeoutError` |
| 409 | `ConflictError` |
| 422 | `UnprocessableEntityError` |
| 429 | `RateLimitError` |
| 500 and above | `InternalServerError` |

A request that gets no answer throws `APIConnectionError`: `APIConnectionTimeoutError` when an attempt took longer than its `timeout`, `APIUserAbortError` when its `signal` aborted it. These, and every other error the client throws itself, are `SdkError`s. A parameter the description does not allow throws `FlowapiRequestError` before anything is sent.

```ts
import { APIError } from 'twilio-studio-sdk'

try {
  await client.flows.list()
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof APIError) console.log(error.status, error.body)
  else throw error
}
```

## Retries and timeouts

A request that cannot connect, or is answered 408, 409, 429 or 5xx, is retried once by default when sending it twice does what sending it once does: its method is GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT or DELETE. A POST or a PATCH that failed may have been applied already, so it is retried only when the server's `x-should-retry: true` asks. The server's `x-should-retry` header decides first, where it sends one; a 403 is never retried. A retry that failed is not tried again: more retries are the caller's choice. Before each retry the client waits as long as the server asks in `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After`, else 0.5 s doubled for each retry made, at most 8 s; when the server asks for more than 60 s, the error is thrown at once. Each attempt may take 60 s, its body read.

`maxRetries`, `timeout` and `maxRetryDelay` change these for the client, the last two in milliseconds; `maxRetries` and `timeout` change them for one call, in its options:

```ts
const patient = new TwilioStudio({ maxRetries: 5, timeout: 120_000 })
await client.flows.list({}, { maxRetries: 0, timeout: 5_000 })
```

## Pagination

A list method is read a page at a time. `for await` over it reads every item, asking for the next page when it needs one; awaited, it gives the first page, with its `items`, `hasNextPage()` and `getNextPage()`. A list stops at 10,000 pages unless `maxPages` says otherwise.

```ts
for await (const item of client.flows.list()) console.log(item)

const page = await client.flows.list()
console.log(page.items, page.hasNextPage())
```

## Logging

The client logs to `console` at `warn` and above. Set `TWILIO_STUDIO_LOG` to `off`, `error`, `warn`, `info` or `debug`, or give `logLevel`: at `info` it writes a line for each attempt, at `debug` the request's URL and headers too, with every credential written as `***`. `logger` sends the lines elsewhere.

```ts
const verbose = new TwilioStudio({ logLevel: 'debug', logger: console })
```

## Requests no method makes

`client.request(method, path, options)` sends a request no operation of the description has, with the client's base URL, credentials, retries and errors; `asResponse()` gives the raw `Response`:

```ts
const response = await client.request('GET', '/').asResponse()
console.log(response.status)
```

## Requirements

Node 20 or later (CI runs 20, 22 and 24), or another runtime with `fetch`. Built with TypeScript 7.0.2.
